INTERACTIVE QUIZZES / PERSONALITY & CHOICES

The Role Behind Your Mask

At a fictional Halloween masquerade, choose what to reveal, what to prepare and what to invent in the moment. Discover the kind of role you would actually want to play.

Results ready
Your results
Your choices

A description of the options you picked in this quiz. It is not a test score, a norm or a diagnosis.

Private Thread
Shared Spotlight

Leaned toward Private Thread. Private Thread favours discoveries exchanged with a few people; Shared Spotlight favours moments the room can experience together. Either can involve leadership, invention and connection.

Prepared Scene
Live Improvisation

Leaned toward Prepared Scene. Prepared Scene favours shaping details in advance; Live Improvisation favours shaping them in response to others. Neither indicates greater creativity or competence.

Task review
Accept a Role

Task 1

You are entrusted with the missing heir’s invitation. How would you most enjoy putting it into the story?

Your choice, no right answer

Your answer: Let a small circle uncover it, then decide together whether to announce it

This choice places your preferred version of this scene along Private Thread–Shared Spotlight. Intimate exchanges and a room-wide moment offer different kinds of involvement.

Original masquerade scenes and descriptive preference mappings, authored for TypologyQuiz (original case written for this quiz)

Task 2

You can shape your courier’s entrance. Which freedom would you choose?

Your choice, no right answer

Your answer: Prepare an opening line and a few facts, leaving the exchange open

This choice places your preferred version of this scene along Prepared Scene–Live Improvisation. Preparation offers a crafted shape; improvisation offers room to respond.

Original masquerade scenes and descriptive preference mappings, authored for TypologyQuiz (original case written for this quiz)

Task 3

Rank the roles you would most want for the next scene, most appealing first.

Your choice, no right answer

Your answer: 1. The table host who draws three guests’ conflicting accounts into one conversation; 2. The confidant who pursues one guest’s hidden reason for borrowing the name; 3. The herald who brings the disputed identity before the whole gathering

This ranking contributes only to Private Thread–Shared Spotlight. Every role has agency; the difference is the size of the moment you share.

Original masquerade scenes and descriptive preference mappings, authored for TypologyQuiz (original case written for this quiz)
Change the Scene

Task 4

Only one version of your discovery can be staged. Which would feel most rewarding?

Your choice, no right answer

Your answer: Let your table hear the response, then carry a short account to the room

This choice places your preferred version of this scene along Private Thread–Shared Spotlight. Intimate exchanges and a room-wide moment offer different kinds of involvement.

Original masquerade scenes and descriptive preference mappings, authored for TypologyQuiz (original case written for this quiz)

Task 5

Your scene partner offers a surprising explanation for the old invitation. What working arrangement would you prefer?

Your choice, no right answer

Your answer: Keep an agreed ending but invent how your characters reach it

This choice places your preferred version of this scene along Prepared Scene–Live Improvisation. Preparation offers a crafted shape; improvisation offers room to respond.

Original masquerade scenes and descriptive preference mappings, authored for TypologyQuiz (original case written for this quiz)

Task 6

Rank these ways of creating a final exchange, most appealing first.

Your choice, no right answer

Your answer: 1. Rehearse the exchange until a small repeated gesture carries the ending; 2. Agree on the final gesture, but leave the words open; 3. Discover both words and gesture by responding to your partner in the moment

This ranking contributes only to Prepared Scene–Live Improvisation. It compares different ways of making the same small scene, with no skill judgment.

Original masquerade scenes and descriptive preference mappings, authored for TypologyQuiz (original case written for this quiz)
Choose Your Last Moment

Task 7

How would you divide your final scene between a private thread and a shared spotlight?

Your choice, no right answer

Your answer: 49 of 100 (0 = An exchange for two, 100 = A moment for the room)

The slider describes where you would place the evening’s final attention. A middle position can preserve both kinds of connection.

Original masquerade scenes and descriptive preference mappings, authored for TypologyQuiz (original case written for this quiz)

Task 8

How much of your next masquerade role would you want to discover while playing it?

Your choice, no right answer

Your answer: 50 of 100 (0 = Shape it beforehand, 100 = Discover it as I play)

This final choice contributes to Prepared Scene–Live Improvisation. Your result combines four contributions per scale; it describes your choices tonight, not a fixed identity.

Original masquerade scenes and descriptive preference mappings, authored for TypologyQuiz (original case written for this quiz)

The Ferry Between Two Promises

Two ghosts wait on opposite shores. Read a cancelled crossing, a borrowed key and two unfinished welcomes to discover why neither stopped waiting. Solve together, then choose an ungraded final line.
